rules.rule: When designing an experiment for agent comparison, define simulation mechanics that explicitly pair distinct agents against the environment to produce aggregated statistical metrics (rates), rather than relying on implicit environment state or raw outcome counts which obscure performance evaluation. This is necessary because baseline comparisons require deterministic, measurable differences in agent behavior across multiple runs.

When designing data flow for analytical plots that require temporal or sequential context, ensure the source interface explicitly defines granular logging (e.g., per-episode or per-step records) rather than only aggregated statistics, because aggregation discards the necessary resolution for time-series visualization. When a baseline in an experiment involves stochastic environment behavior or default agent actions, define it as a configuration mode or wrapper within the execution logic rather than implementing it as a named class module, because baselines are behavioral conditions, not distinct software entities.

When citing experimental outputs that do not yet exist in the file system, describe planned metrics or settings using text and available AST symbol references (\ref_ast) instead of creating non-resolvable CSV pointer links (\ref_csv), because citations must only reference data that is actually present and verifiable at the time of writing.

When generating code that reads external files, use robust path resolution (e.g., via `pathlib` or inspecting `sys.argv`/environment) relative to the script's location or a known configuration root, because relying on the current working directory is fragile and often incorrect in automated execution contexts.
